panels.title: Sapta-Sindhu textual geography
ascii_lines: NORTH-WESTERN MILIEU
Kabul/Kubha ---- Indus/Sindhu ---- Punjab rivers ---- Sarasvati/Drishadvati zone
mountain routes       trunk river       pastoral/farming      eastern attention
v
Rivers organise praise, movement, pasture and conflict; geography is selective.
Ganga is marginal in this horizon; later Vedic expansion shifts the centre east.
Do not turn remembered rivers into precise political borders.
source_references: SESSION 22 - GEOGRAPHY AS A NORTH-WESTERN TEXTUAL MILIEU

panels.title: Kin polity: authority without territorial state
ascii_lines: KULA -> GRAMA -> VIS -> JANA
v
RAJAN: war leadership, protection, distribution and ritual status; not absolute monarch
|-- sabha: smaller/select assembly context | samiti: broader assembly
|-- purohita: adviser | senani: martial role | gramani: group leader
+-> bali: offering/tribute, not a regular land-revenue bureaucracy
Power rested on kin support, cattle, gifts, assemblies and successful leadership.

panels.title: Cattle-agriculture economy loop
ascii_lines: PASTURE + WATER -> CATTLE WEALTH -> dairy, traction, gifts, status and conflict
v
mixed farming: barley/yava + cultivation + crafts + exchange + household production
mobility and raiding              settlement and seasonal cropping
v
Pastoral predominance does not mean absence of agriculture or exchange.

v

panels.title: Early to Later Vedic transformation
ascii_lines: EARLY VEDIC                         LATER VEDIC
north-west/Sapta-Sindhu             upper Ganga-Yamuna and eastward movement
jana and kin leadership             janapada, stronger monarchy and ratnins
cattle-centred mixed economy        plough agriculture, surplus and crafts
fluid differentiation               firmer varna/patriarchy and gotra
deity praise and yajna              royal ritual and Upanishadic questioning
VERDICT: cumulative transformation with regional variation, not abrupt rupture.
source_references: SESSION 16 - HARAPPAN, POST-HARAPPAN AND RIGVEDIC COMPARISON

panels.title: Rig Vedic answer architecture
ascii_lines: 10 MARKS: source caution -> institution/economy -> hymn term -> qualification
15 MARKS: geography -> polity -> economy -> society -> religion -> archaeology caution
20 MARKS: corpus/layers -> Sapta-Sindhu -> kin system -> cattle-agriculture loop
-> differentiation -> ritual worldview -> conflict/contact -> transition
AVOID: nomad-only, caste-complete, state/empire or homogeneous-date claims.
CLOSE: a layered pastoral-agricultural kin society undergoing differentiation.
